text: University Profile; LNU profile; overview of Leyte Normal University. Leyte Normal University (LNU) is a university in Leyte, Philippines, with its main campus in Tacloban City. Its mandate is to provide higher professional and special instruction, promote research and extension, offer advanced studies, and provide progressive leadership in education and related fields. LNU's Quality Policy commits the University to customer satisfaction through good governance, quality and relevant instruction, research, extension and support services, continual improvement of its quality management system, and compliance with ethical, statutory, regulatory, and stakeholder requirements. The Quality Policy was approved under Board of Regents Resolution No. 1189, s. 2019. LNU's core values are Integrity, Excellence, and Service, approved under BOR Resolution No. 705, s. 2015. Integrity includes accountability, honesty, trustworthiness, respect, and ethical conduct; Excellence means persistence and innovative improvement; Service means serving internal and external customers with outstanding service regardless of status, creed, color, or race.

University history; history of Leyte Normal University; founding; establishment; timeline; origins. LNU's teacher-training roots date to School Year 1921–1922, when Leyte High School conducted a two-year normal course to train elementary teachers. The institution became a two-year collegiate teacher-training institution by 1938. In 1952, it became the four-year degree-granting Leyte Normal School. Presidential Decree No. 944 converted Leyte Normal School into Leyte State College on June 14, 1976. Republic Act No. 7901 converted Leyte State College into Leyte Normal University on February 23, 1995. These are historical milestones stated on LNU's official History page.

University charter; LNU charter; Republic Act; mandate; legal basis. LNU's official Charter page identifies Republic Act No. 7910 (1995) as the law converting Leyte State College into a state university to be known as Leyte Normal University. The Charter page says LNU is mandated primarily to provide higher professional and special instruction, promote research and extension services, advanced studies, and progressive leadership in education and other relevant fields. It is authorized to offer undergraduate and graduate courses in education and other related degree courses as the Board of Regents deems necessary to carry out its objectives. The Charter page identifies the main campus as being in Tacloban City. Keep this legal citation attributed to the Charter page; the History page separately lists R.A. 7901 for the conversion milestone.

Vision and mission of Leyte Normal University; university purpose and aspirations. Vision: A globally recognized university of education, management, arts and sciences geared towards the inclusive growth and sustainability of society. Mission: To produce globally recognized human capital along teacher education, management, arts and sciences responsive to the development needs of the society. The LNU Board of Regents approved the Vision and Mission under Resolution No. 1386, s. 2012.

Goals, objectives, and institutional objectives of Leyte Normal University. Four objective areas: Quality and Excellence (meet and exceed stakeholder-defined minimum standards); Relevance and Responsiveness (align academic, research, and extension programs with needs); Access and Equity (provide fair educational opportunities regardless of ethnicity, age, marital, economic or social status, sex, or gender); and Efficiency and Effectiveness (deliver timely, cost-effective, high-impact instruction, research, extension, production, and support services). Institutional objectives: maintain standards as a Center of Excellence within available resources; provide an environment conducive to serious study and research, tolerance, openness, and respect for others' ideas and opinions; and develop God-centered, nationalistic, values-oriented, productive students who contribute to national and global needs. The page attributes institutional objectives to BOR Resolution No. 1189, s. 2019.

University hymn; LNU hymn; song; lyrics; music; melody; composer; lyricist; arranger; audio recording. The official University Hymn page is titled 'Melodies of our Pride.' Credits listed by LNU: Music by Virginio V. Fuentes; lyrics by Rosario P. Isiderio; arrangement by Manuel Flores; enhancement and rearrangement by Gilbert William Salazar. The official page contains the hymn lyrics. When asked for the lyrics, present them in complete verse lines with stanza spacing, a centered Lyrics heading, the closing university name emphasized, and credits below, followed by the official page link. No playable audio or direct audio-file link is exposed on the official page; do not invent an audio URL.
